title: ‘Racism and Misogyny’: Photographer Misan Harriman Talks About the Media Attacks on his Friend Meghan Markle
author: Sangita Myska
content:
_**Editor 's note:** We thought you might find **Zeteo UK contributor Sangita
Myska 's** interview with the renowned photographer and activist Misan
Harriman on the new podcast, **' Sangita Meets…'** a worthwhile watch, so
we're sharing it with all **Zeteo** subscribers today._

_Paid**Zeteo** subscribers can watch this episode in full, but to access all

In just eight years since **Misan Harriman** took up photography, his photos
have become some of the most iconic images of global protest movements from[
Black Lives Matter](https://www.vogue.co.uk/news/gallery/black-lives-matter-
protest-6-june) to[ climate
change](https://www.instagram.com/p/DaBhrEojDWk/?img_index=1),[
LGBTQ+](https://www.instagram.com/p/DaX5S8yDNYw/) and[ pro-
Palestine](https://www.instagram.com/p/DdrFiooDBw_/) rallies. In August 2020,
he made history as the first Black male photographer to shoot a cover for[
British Vogue](https://www.vogue.co.uk/news/article/misan-harriman-vogue-
cover).

And in this episode of '**Sangita Meets …**', Misan speaks to **Sangita
Myska** about what drove him to pick up the camera. **" Watching somebody that
looks like me, George Floyd, lying in his own piss, asking for his mama, while
still calling the men who had [a knee] on his neck, sir, as he left his mortal
coil … The choice was already made for me,"** he says.

In this personal and in-depth interview, Sangita also asks Misan - who has
taken [intimate portraits](https://substack.com/home/post/p-181368158) of
Prince Harry, Meghan Markle, and [their
children](https://www.instagram.com/p/CeelNvSgZJB/?hl=en&img_index=1) - about
how the British media has treated the Duke and Duchess of Sussex. **" There is
a healthy dose of good old fashioned misogyny, misogynoir, racism,"** he says.
**" It's a combination of greed as well because…that hate sells. It feeds an
algorithm that's designed for that."**

Misan also opens up on:

  * The **" poison pen"** of the press and its culpability in the tragic suicide death of Cambridge Professor Jason Arday, following what critics call a relentless, and[ often racist](https://www.bbc.com/news/articles/clyxklg3xypo), media frenzy over his academic record

  * The vicious[ online campaign](https://www.middleeasteye.net/news/record-complaints-filed-over-uk-press-smear-anti-genocide-pro-palestine-artist-misan-harriman) against him over his support for Gaza and criticisms of Israel (**" The forensic scraping of any story posts, any collabs, any shares … It means that they would have seen my advocacy with multiple Jewish groups."**)

  * How he responds to criticisms that he's part of the British elite

  * What it feels like to have someone else tell his own story, in the documentary about his life, 'Shoot the People'.
